title: Anxiety follows borrowed greatness
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 188
summary: The shabad opens by stripping the glamour from worldly greatness and naming its hidden disease: anxiety. It then asks what greatness means at all and answers with loving attachment to the Lord.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person pulled into status, land, ownership, or the need to look weighty. Kept near, it changes the measure of greatness from possession to devotion.
takeaway: Let this stay with you: choose the Lord's measure of greatness and refuse Maya's scale.

lines.translation: Those who seem to be great and powerful,
are afflicted by the disease of anxiety. ||1||
Who is great by the greatness of Maya?

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਵਡਾ ਜਿਨਿ ਰਾਮ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਈ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: so vaddaa jin raam liv laiee ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: They alone are great, who are lovingly attached to the Lord. ||1||Pause||
The landlord fights over his land each day.
He shall have to leave it in the end, and yet his desire is still not satisfied. ||2||
Says Nanak, this is the essence of Truth:
without the Lord's meditation, there is no salvation. ||3||44||113||

structure: First, it begins by exposing the anxiety hidden inside visible greatness.
Then, it shows desire still raging even in the one who appears established and secure.
Finally, it ends in essence: without devotion to the Lord, there is no real release.
